title: SIEM export: degraded-mode mitigation and field compatibility playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a conservative, interoperable approach for exporting audit and evidence events to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, Sentinel) with special guidance for degraded-mode operation, RBAC v2 field considerations, evidence automation triggers, and connector-level compatibility transforms. It is intended for engineering owners of SIEM connectors, SREs, and security product managers.

Scope:
- Audit log schema baseline and versioning policy.
- Field-level mapping conventions and required/optional fields for downstream SIEMs.
- Degraded-mode behaviours (backpressure, buffering, staged delivery, fallback storage).
- PII/PHI redaction rules and per-customer opt-in exemptions.
- Evidence automation hooks and acknowledgement semantics.
- Concrete payload examples for Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, and Azure Sentinel ingestion.

Key design principles:
1) Forward/backward compatibility: always include a schema_version field at the top-level event and avoid renaming existing required fields; introduce new fields using "extra.*" namespace to avoid collisions.
2) Idempotency & deduplication: every exported event must include event_id (UUIDv4) and a monotonic ingestion_seq when applicable to help downstream dedupe.
3) Minimal required surface: for most SIEMs send a compact canonical event; attach full_record only when allowed by customer retention policy.
4) Privacy-first defaults: redact sensitive fields by default; allow customer-managed allowlists via contract + KMS policy.
5) Graceful degradation: when real-time export fails, persist to durable staging (S3 encryption + manifest) and switch connectors to batch mode.

Schema baseline (recommended canonical fields):
- schema_version: string, e.g. "2025-10-01" (required)
- event_id: string (UUIDv4) (required)
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC (required)
- org_id: string (Redwood org id) (required)
- project: string (product area or customer project) (optional)
- actor: string (redwood user id or service identity) (optional)
- actor_ip: string (IPv4/IPv6) (optional, subject to redaction)
- action: string (high level verb, e.g., "model.deploy", "siem.export.send") (required)
- resource: string (resource path or id) (optional)
- outcome: string (success|failure|partial) (required)
- severity: string (informational|low|medium|high|critical) (optional)
- details: string (short human readable summary) (optional)
- full_record: string (base64 gzipped JSON of the complete event for evidence automation; only present when customer consent/contract allows) (optional)
- extra.<key>: arbitrary key/values for future data (optional)

RBAC v2 & field-level access notes:
- When exporting events that contain RBAC decision context, include rbac_policy_version and rbac_grant_set (list of granted actions) in extra.rbac.*. Do NOT include full policy documents unless explicitly requested and encrypted.
- Field exposure must follow per-customer RBAC mapping: connectors should consult the per-org allowlist before including actor_email or scope_ids.
- Evidence automation events that trigger a downstream workflow must include evidence_level (low|standard|forensic) so SIEM runbooks can escalate differently.

Evidence automation and acknowledgement semantics:
- Trigger event: an evidence event is exported with evidence_request_id and evidence_level and a delivery_ack_required boolean.
- Acknowledgement path: When delivery_ack_required=true, the connector must wait for a delivery_ack (ack_event_id) from the SIEM ack endpoint (where supported) or mark acknowledged after durable storage confirmation.
- Retry semantics: exponential backoff up to (configurable) 72 hours; after max retries surface to customer ops with manifest link.

Degraded-mode behaviours (recommended):
1) Transient outage (downstream HTTP 5xx or rate limits): switch to local in-memory queue for short windows (<=60s) with circuit breaker and then to S3 staging when queue > threshold.
2) Sustained outage (>5 minutes): flip connector to batch push from S3 staging at lower throughput; notify customer via configured webhooks/email.
3) Unrecoverable degradation: mark events with outcome=partial and include degraded_reason and degraded_since fields; generate a daily manifest for customer review.
4) Backpressure handling: honor upstream per-customer rate limits and avoid dropping audit records — prefer delayed delivery with preservation guarantees.

Connector-specific guidance:
- Splunk (HTTP Event Collector - HEC):
  - Best-effort layout: send each canonical event as a single HEC JSON with fields: time, host (org_id), source ("redwood:audits"), sourcetype ("_json"), event (canonical event JSON).
  - Recommended header: Authorization: Splunk <HEC-TOKEN>, X-Redwood-Connector-Version: <version>.
  - Compression: enable gzip for batch uploads.
  - Error handling: HTTP 429 -> respect Retry-After header; HTTP 400 for invalid JSON -> write to quarantine bucket and create ticket.
  - Example payload: {
    "time": 1696224000,
    "host": "org-123",
    "source": "redwood:audits",
    "sourcetype": "_json",
    "event": {"schema_version":"2025-10-01","event_id":"...","action":"model.deploy", ...}
  }

- Datadog Logs API:
  - Preferred format: Datadog recommends one JSON per log; include ddsource: "redwood-audit" and ddtags: "org:org-123,env:prod" in the attributes.
  - API constraints: 5MB per request; recommend batching 500 events or by size.
  - PII tagging: include metadata.pii=true where fields contain PII so customers can apply built-in scrubbing rules on Datadog side.
  - Example header: Content-Type: application/json, DD-API-KEY: <key>.

- Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics / Event Hub):
  - Two ingestion patterns supported: direct Log Analytics Data Collector API (post to custom table) or via Event Hub/Forwarder into Sentinel.
  - For Log Analytics: map canonical fields to a custom table schema. Use schema_version as a column to support view-based migrations.
  - For Event Hub: publish JSON batches with partition key = org_id to guarantee ordering per tenant.
  - Authentication: prefer Managed Identity / Service Principal with secret rotation.

Field mapping & transform rules (connector behaviour):
- Canonical->Splunk: flatten nested objects into extra.* dot-notation (extra.rbac.grants[0]) and avoid arrays deeper than 2 levels; use JSON stringification for complex nested objects.
- Canonical->Datadog: keep structured JSON, but replace binary full_record with a reference_url if >64KB.
- Canonical->Sentinel: map full_record to a blob pointer (SAS url) rather than inlining large payloads.

PII/PHI redaction and redact metadata:
- Redaction categories: ip_address, email, username, ssn, credit_card, medical_id.
- Default action: replace with token <REDACTED:category>. Maintain redaction_summary array in extra.redaction_summary listing which fields were redacted and reason.
- Customer exemptions: when contract includes forensic-evidence allowlist, full_record may be included encrypted with customer-managed key (CMK). Document encryption envelope and KMS key id in extra.kms_metadata.

Operational runbook (for SREs and connector owners):
- Daily sanity checks: verify recent export rate vs expected, monitor last_successful_export timestamp per org, alert if >1hr behind for high-volume customers.
- Incident triage checklist:
  1) Check connector health (uptime, queue depth, S3 staging size).
  2) Inspect last 50 HTTP responses; identify 4xx vs 5xx patterns.
  3) If 429s observed, adjust batching/parallelism and honor Retry-After.
  4) For schema errors (400): identify event_id(s), move to quarantine, create PR for schema stabilization if systemic.
  5) Restore from staging: ensure rehydration respects original timestamps and event ordering when possible.

Testing and validation matrix (minimum):
- Unit tests for: schema_version parsing, redaction engine, batching logic, idempotency handling.
- Integration tests: simulate downstream 429/5xx and validate degraded-mode S3 staging and replay.
- End-to-end: on-boarding flow for a test org with Splunk, Datadog, Sentinel endpoints; include retention/consent permutations.

Appendix: example event (canonical)
{
  "schema_version": "2025-10-01",
  "event_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-04T14:33:22Z",
  "org_id": "org-123",
  "action": "audit.export",
  "outcome": "success",
  "severity": "informational",
  "details": "Exported evidence bundle to customer SIEM (HEC) in batch mode.",
  "extra.rbac_policy_version": "v2.1",
  "extra.evidence_level": "forensic",
  "full_record": "<base64 gzipped JSON>",
  "degraded_reason": "",
  "degraded_since": ""
}

Notes & next steps:
- Product: finalise customer-facing allowlist/opt-in templates for full_record sharing.
- Engineering: implement schema_version gate in connectors to reject unsupported older schema with a clear failure code.
- Security: publish a short runbook for customers describing what to expect in a degraded export and how to acknowledge evidence receipts.

This playbook is intentionally prescriptive in the areas that impact customer compliance and incident post-mortem readiness. Feedback welcome — add comments in the confluence:SEC-EXPORT-2025 page and link tickets to jira:SEC-2345.
